edge_cases: Missing required fields in POST /add_book results in a server error (e.g., KeyError)
Updating a non‑existent book_id still returns a success message but changes no rows
Searching with an empty keyword returns all rows (or none if the table is empty)
Providing an empty genre in /get_books_by_genre returns no rows
SQL injection is possible because query strings are built via string interpolation
Very large request bodies may cause SQLite or Flask to raise errors
contract.intent: Expose a RESTful HTTP API that lets clients add, search, update, delete, and list books stored in a SQLite 'library.db' database.
invariants: All responses are JSON-encoded and include an HTTP status code as defined above
Each book row contains the columns id, title, author, and genre
Database connections are always closed before the request handler returns
The API does not perform authentication or authorization
io_behavior: POST /add_book with JSON {title, author, genre} → 201 and JSON {"message":"Book added successfully"}
GET /search_books?keyword=… → 200 and JSON array of books whose title or author contains the keyword
PUT /update_book/<book_id> with JSON {title?, author?, genre?} → 200 and JSON {"message":"Book updated successfully"}
GET /get_books_by_genre?genre=… → 200 and JSON array of books matching the genre
side_effects: Writes to the file 'library.db' (inserts, updates, deletes rows)
Creates 'library.db' if it does not already exist
Opens a network socket to listen for HTTP requests
Closes the SQLite connection after each request

rationale: Core routes and responses match contract, connections closed, side‑effects present; however missing‑field handling and SQL‑injection protection diverge from specified edge cases.
